Alice: Quick summary — I ran the kernel selector bump on canary and we're seeing a correlated drop in KV prefix cache hit-rate.
Ben: numbers?
Alice: Quick numbers from the canary window:
- before (kernel_v3): prefix cache hit 78%, p95 34ms, tokens/s 12k
- after  (kernel_v4): prefix cache hit 62%, p95 52ms, tokens/s 11.2k
Also ~3x more cold-model hits (no KV) during the first 10m after rollout.
Maya: Interesting. Did seq-length distribution change? I know v4 switches to tiled attention for >512 and that can change batching boundaries.
Alice: Median seq len is basically the same, but batching boundary alignment shifted slightly which looks like it changes how we break prompts into probe chunks -> different probe keys.
Ben: Could this be a tokenizer offset change? If kernel path changes how we chunk tokens, the prefix fingerprint can diverge.
Alice: That's my hypothesis. Repro curl I used (canary):
```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/serve -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-large","prompt":"<user prompt here>","runtime_flags":{"kernel":"v4"}}'
```
Carla: Another note: in PR #1423 we changed a tiny whitespace normalization for prefix normalization and also flipped the kernel selection flag. Might be two orthogonal diffs combining.
Ben: We should confirm what fields are part of the cache key. Does the key include tokenizer version and kernel_id today?
Maya: Batching heuristics in v4 also changed: dynamic batch flush at 8ms instead of 12ms -> more micro-batches, so fewer aggregated requests and less opportunity for warm KV hits within the same batch window.
Alice: So two mechanisms: key divergence (tokenization/chunking/normalization) and fewer batching coalesces leading to colder caches.
Carla: I checked — PR 2190 added tokenizer.version into the key for new models but it was gated off for legacy routing. rwd-large didn't get the tag.
Ben: Actionable quick fixes we can try:
1) Ensure cache key includes tokenizer_version + kernel_id to avoid silent mismatches.
2) Run targeted warmup issuing top-N prefixes using the exact runtime flags (kernel_v4) to prepopulate cache.
3) Add per-kernel telemetry: prefix_key -> kernel_id mapping and per-kernel hit-rate.
perf-bot: warmup-run finished @ 12:08 — synthetic warmup script (top-2k prefixes) ran for 7m, observed synthetic hit-rate uplift +18ppt in canary env after warmup.
Maya: Also consider kernel-aware prefetch: when a node boots with kernel_v4, run a prefetch for front-page prefixes transformed with the v4 tokenizer pipeline so first real requests see hits.
Alice: Logging snippet to add (for telemetry + audit):
```
log.info("prefetch", {"prefix_hash": prefix_hash, "kernel": kernel_id, "tokenizer": tok_version, "warmup_src": "kernel_prefetch"})
```
Ben: I'll open a small hotfix to re-enable the tokenizer tag for rwd-large and wire the kernel_id into the key + telemetry. PR target: hotfix/cachekey-kernel-2196.
Ben: Experiment plan: route 10% traffic to kernel_v4 + run warmup tool; measure hit-rate for 1h. Rollback if p95 > 45ms or overall hit-rate < 70%.
Maya: I'll own the warmup run and scheduling. Will post metrics after the 1h window. :thumbsup:
Alice: tagging @eng-sre for any capacity/regression impact on canary pools.
Carla: FYI we should also add an integration check in our perf CI: after kernel selection changes run a short warmup sim and assert prefix hit-rate delta < 5ppt.
Ben: Agreed. Short-term hotfix + warmup, mid-term add kernel-aware prefetch and CI guard.
Alice: Thanks all, will watch the A/B and collect traces.
